هذه الطريقة تكون ملائمة لتقدير الحموضة للزيوت المستعملة او الغير مستعملة مثل 
 زيوت التسحيم وزيوت الوقود اما زيوت البترول المحتوية على اضافات فانه من 
 الممكن ان تعطى نتائج غير سليمة

توجد 3 طرق لقياس الحموضة IP1 
 طريقة (A),(B),(C)
 الطريقة (A) 
 , (B) 
 تعيين الحموضة الكلية ولكن الطريقة (A) 
 اكثر ملائمة من الطريقة (B) 
 بالنسبة للزيوت القاتمة اللون والزيوت التى لها لزوجة عالية اكثر من 120 سنتى 
 ستوك عند 100 F

الطريقة (B) 
 يفضل استخدامها فى الزيوت الشفافة وذات اللزوجة المنخفضة مثل زيوت المحولات, 
 الطريقة (C) 
 تستخدم فى قياس الحموضة الغير عضوية.

قام بإعداد هذا المستند الكيميائية/ 
 سهير عبد الوارث حسن وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/

 اشرف صلاح الدين صالح وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/

sections_en.text: This method is suitable for determining the acidity of used or unused oils, such as lubricating oils and fuel oils; however, petroleum oils containing additives may give incorrect results.

There are 3 methods for measuring acidity, IP1 methods (A), (B) and (C). Methods (A) and (B) determine total acidity, but method (A) is more suitable than method (B) for dark-coloured oils and oils with a high viscosity of more than 120 centistokes at 100°F.
Method (B) is preferably used for transparent, low-viscosity oils such as transformer oils. Method (C) is used to measure inorganic acidity.

This document was prepared by the chemist Soheir Abdel Wareth Hassan, reviewed by the chemist Khaled Bastawy Makki Mohasseb, tested by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: Determination of the total acidity of new oil to check its conformity with the specifications.
Determination of the total acidity of used oil to determine the extent of oil oxidation during operation.
Determining the efficiency of the oil during operation.

To determine the total acidity of the sample, the sample is dissolved in a suitable solvent (a mixture of toluene and ethanol) and titrated with a 0.1 N alkaline solution of KOH. To determine the inorganic acidity, the sample is extracted with hot distilled water and the extract is titrated with a 0.1 N alkaline solution.
It is a measure of the sum of both organic acidity and inorganic acidity.
Total acidity:
It is a measure of the mineral acids present in the oil.
Inorganic acidity:
It is obtained by subtracting the inorganic acidity from the total acidity.
Organic acidity:
Place the chemicals used in well-ventilated cabinets, in places away from flames.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor or on the balance; if this happens, remove it.
Graduated pipette 1 ml (each division 0.01 ml) - 250 ml conical flask - volumetric flask - 100 ml graduated cylinder - sensitive balance.
0.1 N alcoholic potassium hydroxide - 95% ethyl alcohol - 0.1 N HCl.
Toluene - alkaline blue indicator.

sections_en.text: Steps for preparing the alkaline blue indicator

rows: Extract 2 g of the alkaline blue indicator with boiling alcohol using a Soxhlet apparatus
Filter if necessary, then dilute to 100 ml with alcohol.
Weigh 10 g of oil in a 250 ml conical flask.
Mix 60 ml of toluene + 40 ml of 95% ethyl alcohol in another conical flask.
Add 1-3 ml of the alkaline blue indicator + a drop of 0.1 N HCl to the above mixture to make the indicator more sensitive, obtaining a blue-violet colour.
Neutralize the mixture with 0.1 N KOH solution until a red-violet colour is obtained.
Add the neutralized mixture to the oil sample with continuous stirring until a blue-violet colour is obtained.

After the sample has completely dissolved, titrate immediately using alcoholic KOH solution at a temperature not exceeding 30°C, until the colour changes from blue-violet to red-violet and remains so for 15 seconds, or changes back to blue on adding two drops of 0.1 N HCl.
Record the volume of potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration.
The total acidity (AT) is calculated from the following equation:
V = volume of alcoholic potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration; N = normality of alcoholic potassium hydroxide, 0.1 N; W = weight of the oil sample to be tested, in grams
Reproducibility for Method A
Repeatability for Method A

Introduction
This method is suitable for determining the acidity of used or unused oils, such as lubricating oils and fuel oils; however, petroleum oils containing additives may give incorrect results.
There are 3 methods for measuring acidity, IP1 methods (A), (B) and (C). Methods (A) and (B) determine total acidity, but method (A) is more suitable than method (B) for dark-coloured oils and oils with a high viscosity of more than 120 centistokes at 100°F.
Method (B) is preferably used for transparent, low-viscosity oils such as transformer oils. Method (C) is used to measure inorganic acidity.
This document was prepared by the chemist Soheir Abdel Wareth Hassan, reviewed by the chemist Khaled Bastawy Makki Mohasseb, tested by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
Determination of the total acidity of new oil to check its conformity with the specifications. | 
Determination of the total acidity of used oil to determine the extent of oil oxidation during operation. | 
Determining the efficiency of the oil during operation. | 
Summary of Method
To determine the total acidity of the sample, the sample is dissolved in a suitable solvent (a mixture of toluene and ethanol) and titrated with a 0.1 N alkaline solution of KOH. To determine the inorganic acidity, the sample is extracted with hot distilled water and the extract is titrated with a 0.1 N alkaline solution. | 
Definition
It is a measure of the sum of both organic acidity and inorganic acidity. | Total acidity: | 
It is a measure of the mineral acids present in the oil. | Inorganic acidity: | 
It is obtained by subtracting the inorganic acidity from the total acidity. | Organic acidity: | 
Environmental Recommendations
Place the chemicals used in well-ventilated cabinets, in places away from flames. | 1.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor or on the balance; if this happens, remove it. | 2.
Tools and Materials Used
Graduated pipette 1 ml (each division 0.01 ml) - 250 ml conical flask - volumetric flask - 100 ml graduated cylinder - sensitive balance. | 1.
0.1 N alcoholic potassium hydroxide - 95% ethyl alcohol - 0.1 N HCl. | 2.
Toluene - alkaline blue indicator. | 3.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Steps for preparing the alkaline blue indicator
Extract 2 g of the alkaline blue indicator with boiling alcohol using a Soxhlet apparatus | 1.
Filter if necessary, then dilute to 100 ml with alcohol. | 2.
Test Steps
Method A
Weigh 10 g of oil in a 250 ml conical flask. | 1.
Mix 60 ml of toluene + 40 ml of 95% ethyl alcohol in another conical flask. | 2.
Add 1-3 ml of the alkaline blue indicator + a drop of 0.1 N HCl to the above mixture to make the indicator more sensitive, obtaining a blue-violet colour. | 3.
Neutralize the mixture with 0.1 N KOH solution until a red-violet colour is obtained. | 4.
Add the neutralized mixture to the oil sample with continuous stirring until a blue-violet colour is obtained. | 5.
After the sample has completely dissolved, titrate immediately using alcoholic KOH solution at a temperature not exceeding 30°C, until the colour changes from blue-violet to red-violet and remains so for 15 seconds, or changes back to blue on adding two drops of 0.1 N HCl. | 6.
Record the volume of potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration. | 7.
